ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$. If $\angle B=108^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in the circle $\odot O$, and $\angle B=108^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle D=180^\circ-\angle B=180^\circ-108^\circ=\boxed{72^\circ}$.

Reasoning: It is known that ∠B = 108°. Because ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so ∠B + ∠D = 180°. Therefore ∠D = 180° - 108° = 72°.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a circle with chords AB, BC, CD, and DA forming an inscribed quadrilateral. Interpret ∠B as the inscribed angle subtending arc ADC, and ∠D as the inscribed angle subtending the remaining arc ABC. Since the two intercepted arcs together make the full circle, their measures sum to 360°. By the inscribed angle theorem, the corresponding angles sum to half of 360°, or 180°. Thus ∠D = 180° − ∠B = 180° − 108° = 72°.
